description: We are a team of 6th-grade students, together with our supervisors.
summary:
Moon Miner Game
Moon Miner is an educational Scratch game that lets players run their own lunar mission. Players earn their funding by answering a space-science quiz, use that money to buy rocket components, assemble a rocket and launch it to the Moon. After they land, explore the lunar surface to find and collect resources and return to earth. 
The problem:
Space exploration is exciting, but for many students it feels distant. They see launches on video, yet rarely understand what stands behind a mission: knowledge, funding, engineering and the search for resources beyond Earth. We wanted to give young people a way to experience that chain of decisions instead of only reading about it.
Our solution:
Moon Miner is a game-based simulation built in Scratch. Every stage of the game mirrors a real stage of a space mission:
1.Earn funding – the knowledge quiz. Players answer questions about space, the Moon and rocket science. Correct answers bring in money for the mission. The message is simple: knowledge is what makes exploration possible.
2.Buy components. With the funds earned, players visit the shop to buy rocket parts. 
3.Build the rocket. Players assemble the parts into a working rocket and prepare it for launch.
4.Launch and flight. The rocket lifts off and travels to the Moon in a 24-second flight sequence.
5.Land and explore. After landing, players move across the lunar surface to search for and collect resources.
6.Return and get a million for yourself.
